summary: Pointing -i at a directory loads multiple inventory sources at once, mixing dynamic (executable) and static files. Files ending in ~, .orig, .bak, .ini, .cfg, .retry, .pyc, .pyo are ignored unless you change inventory_ignore_extensions; group_vars and host_vars there work.
questions: Can I combine static and dynamic inventory in one run?
Why is my .ini file ignored in an inventory directory?
How do I change which files Ansible ignores in an inventory folder?
Can I use group_vars inside an inventory directory?

answer_card.title: Inventory directories and multiple sources
answer_card.answer_md:
If `-i` (or `ansible.cfg`) points to a directory, every source in it is used: executables as dynamic inventory, most other files as static.

Ignored by default: `~, .orig, .bak, .ini, .cfg, .retry, .pyc, .pyo`. Change with `inventory_ignore_extensions` in `ansible.cfg` or `ANSIBLE_INVENTORY_IGNORE` (comma-separated patterns).

`group_vars/` and `host_vars/` subdirectories work as expected.
